lines.story-0: Every picture NASA makes of our planet is a measurement. Tonight, we turn those measurements into music. Every note you hear is read, pixel by pixel, from maps made by NASA's Earth Information Center.
lines.story-1: This is the ocean: currents and sea temperature. We read the colour of every pixel through NASA's own colour key, and turn temperature into pitch. Warm tropical water sings high on the cello. Cold polar water sinks low.
lines.story-2: Here is the Gulf Stream, carrying the warmth of the tropics north. Hear how the notes rise as we follow it.
lines.story-3: Now the rain, from NASA's weather model, just days ago. Each patch of rain plucks a note on the flute. The heavier the rain, the more notes fall. Thick clouds become the soft pad underneath. This is the monsoon over India.
lines.story-4: This is lightning, seen from the International Space Station. Watch the golden needle. As it sweeps the map, every flash it touches becomes a violin note. Higher on the map is a higher note. Further east, and the sound moves to your right.
lines.story-5: Together, the planet plays in tune. Every Earth sound is held to one musical key, A major, the key our instruments were recorded in. Underneath, a slow chord progression holds it all together.
lines.story-6: Now, listen to us. City lights at night, from 2012 to 2023. We give humanity notes that clash with the planet's key. The brighter the city, the more the clarinet cuts through.
lines.story-7: Carbon emissions become a low, heavy drone. Nitrogen oxides from traffic and industry become a rough reed, pushing against the harmony. The more pollution, the louder it grows.
lines.story-8: This is home. Bahrain and the Gulf, up close. NASA sees our whole island in just a handful of twenty-kilometre squares. But listen: warm seas, bright cities, and the hum of industry, all playing at once.
lines.story-9: Now, let's do something no one can do in real life. Let's mute humanity.
lines.story-10: Listen. This is the Earth, in tune. The ocean, the rain, the storms. Still here. Still singing.
lines.story-11: The lever is yours now. Bring us back, a little or a lot, and hear the difference. Pick a record, zoom anywhere, and listen to our planet.
lines.mode-listen: Listen. You hear everything on the screen. Zoom in to hear one place.
lines.mode-scan: Scan. A needle sweeps across the map. Higher on the screen is a higher note.
lines.mode-probe: Probe. Click anywhere, and I'll tell you what's there.
lines.mute: Humanity muted. This is the planet without us.
lines.bahrain-open: Bahrain, up close. NASA's maps see the world in squares about twenty kilometres wide, so our whole island is only a handful of them. Everything you hear now comes from just this corner of the Gulf.
lines.near-the-north-pacific-garbage-patch: Near the North Pacific garbage patch.
